basics.name: Chenming Ge
basics.summary: Human–Computer Interaction, Generative UI, Computer-use Agents, and Human–AI Interaction

work.summary: Detecting accessibility failures that emerge during interaction, beyond what a static page check can reveal.
highlights: Developed a taxonomy of navigation failures affecting blind and low-vision screen-reader users, drawing on prior literature and user studies.
Formalized navigation failures as Linear Temporal Logic (LTL) properties and implemented checks over interface interactions.
Built a web-agent baseline that navigates through screen-reader feedback and keyboard-only interaction.
Evaluated the checker on generated websites, achieving 88.7% precision.

work.summary: Studying how interaction traces can help AI-generated interfaces become more usable.
highlights: Built a pipeline to generate websites, collect interaction traces from user studies, identify usability issues, and repair interfaces using the resulting critiques.
Implemented Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) to fine-tune models for generating more usable interfaces.
Explored computer-use agents and coding agents as baselines for simulating user behavior and providing usability feedback.
work.name: Reinforcement Learning from Interactive Experience and Feedback

work.summary: Helping web agents transfer what they learn as websites and interfaces change.
highlights: Built an adversarial co-evolution framework that pairs a coding-agent-driven UI drift generator with a web agent.
Extracted generalizable reflection rules from agent failures and compared them with an ExpeL baseline.
Worked on a knowledge-graph pipeline to identify tasks affected by website version changes.
Containerized multiple website versions with Docker using BrowserGym and AgentLab.

publications.name: A11yLTLNav: Automatic Detection of Accessibility Navigation Failures
